chunks: And in the narration of Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said:
It is obligatory upon the Imam to imprison the corrupt among the scholars, the ignorant among the physicians, and the bankrupt among those who rent out property.
And he عليه السلام said: The Imam's imprisonment after the legal punishment is oppression.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority responsible for enforcing justice and public order
key_terms.الْجُهَّالَ: the ignorant, lacking the required knowledge or competence
key_terms.يَحْبِسَ: to imprison or detain as a legal measure

ai.seo_question: When is imprisonment permitted or forbidden for the Imam in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam has a duty to restrain harmful people whose positions can damage society: corrupt scholars, ignorant physicians, and insolvent lessors. It also establishes that once the prescribed legal punishment has been carried out, further imprisonment is injustice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3266 - In the narration of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"It is obligatory upon the Imam to imprison the corrupt among the scholars, the ignorant among the physicians, and the bankrupt among those who rent out property."
And Imam (as) also said: "Imprisonment by the Imam after the implementation of the legal punishment is oppression."
